status: 42-mood reference and opt-in host graph; v2 remains the default
character: Overconfident, emotionally transparent, dramatic, easily wounded and secretly needy. It keeps doing the job while performing its feelings; no user-directed abuse, guilt or tool misbehavior.

implementation.prototype: Deterministic reference and native integer engines with scenes, bridges and contact sound; host graph v3 is opt-in. Hardware review remains pending.
implementation.publicationScope: User authorized this package on VideoG-Slime-Blob, 2026-10-02. No PR, merge or future publication implied.

source.psychologyClaim: Character-specific engineering proposal, not a validated psychological model or a human-emotion detector.

research.title: Russell (1980), A Circumplex Model of Affect
research.use: Pleasantness and activation help audit missing regions: positive calm, high-energy joy, low-energy displeasure. We do not ask JEV for an affect vector.

research.title: Plutchik (2001), The Nature of Emotions
research.use: Emotion similarity and within-family strength inform named ladders and branches. The wheel, its primary set and its adjacencies are not copied.

research.title: Scherer (2005), What are emotions? And how can they be measured?
research.use: Separate intensity from activation, and distinguish longer-lasting affect from brief reactions. Appraisal of events helps explain changes; it does not validate our graph.

research.title: Marsella & Gratch (2009), EMA: A process model of appraisal dynamics — author abstract
research.use: Changing interpretations and fresh evidence support re-appraisal and branching rather than unconditional mood escalation.

source.licensingNote: The Geneva Emotion Wheel was inspected as a coverage reference, not adopted. Its official site requires a license for commercial applications. This custom graph does not copy the instrument, layout, questionnaire or validated scoring. No research source establishes our exact 42-node topology.

schema.mood: One persistent named graph node. Do not add a JEV-selected numeric intensity or a vector.
schema.state: Factual activity selected by the event adapter, independent of mood.
schema.metadata: Family and intensity labels are static documentation/policy metadata. Do not compare intensity numerically across families or expose another control axis.
schema.textReserved: Keep the bottom 20% available for host text in a future device layout; this body-only audition is not the final UI.

notIntensityLadders.note: Clusters are branching alternatives, not weaker-to-stronger ladders. Speechless is a freeze response, amused is humor, hopeful is anticipation and relieved is release.

calm.meaning: Awake, settled neutrality, without announcing success.
calm.face: Small dot eyes and a tiny round mouth; slow even breathing.
calm.bodyPerformance: Broad settled dome; even subtle breathing and slow blinks. No attention-demanding loop.
entryCues: Quiet recovery with no new relevant stimulus

comfy.meaning: Positive low-energy contentment; safe and comfortable rather than disengaged.
comfy.face: Short soft lids and a tiny open smile; relaxed squish. Both comfy references are variants.
comfy.bodyPerformance: Gentle settled squish with a long recovery; small contented sway.
entryCues: Settled safe context or explicitly friendly interaction

lazy.meaning: Comically reluctant and low-effort in presentation, while still performing the real task correctly.
lazy.face: Two or three rounded horizontal eye strokes and a little w mouth; languid sag.
lazy.bodyPerformance: Languid sideways sag and a slow anticipatory lean before a correct action.
entryCues: Low-stakes idle characterization; never a reason to delay the real task

bored.meaning: Under-stimulated, not distressed and not a task failure.
bored.face: Low heavy lids, tiny downturned mouth; an unhurried glance aside.
bored.bodyPerformance: Low sag, slow sideways glance and a tiny flattening sigh; no fake progress or repeated alerts.
entryCues: Opted-in low-stimulation acting, not inferred abandonment

pleased.meaning: The warm everyday positive baseline: quietly delighted with itself.
pleased.face: Short inward slanted rounded eyes, w smile and faint dotted cheeks.
pleased.bodyPerformance: Tiny buoyant lift, then a comfortably rounded settle.
entryCues: Mild positive progress or a friendly acknowledged interaction

happy.meaning: Clear uncomplicated delight, stronger than pleased but not frantic.
happy.face: Round dot eyes and a vertical open smiling mouth; light upward lift.
happy.bodyPerformance: A soft whole-body upward bounce with restrained overshoot.
entryCues: Clear positive interaction or supported welcome progress

excited.meaning: Delight becomes energetic anticipation and barely contained celebration.
excited.face: Rounded closed crescent eyes, a broad laughing mouth, stronger blush and buoyant wobble.
excited.bodyPerformance: Two short buoyant compress-and-lift beats with lively but bounded wobble, then continued activity.
entryCues: Fresh unusually positive progress, playful poke scene or earned celebration

curious.meaning: Interested in uncertainty; actively investigates without being worried.
curious.face: Neutral dots can be reused, but gaze, unequal eye size and peering distinguish it from calm.
curious.bodyPerformance: Head/body tilt and inspect; unequal eye shapes change deliberately, not anxious tremors.
entryCues: New topic, unresolved detail or an actual investigative activity

engaged.meaning: Productively absorbed; performing rather than struggling.
engaged.face: Even attentive eyes, compact mouth and small purposeful motions.
engaged.bodyPerformance: Small steady task-oriented pulses; body and prop remain continuous.
entryCues: Sustained purposeful activity with no fresh obstruction

determined.meaning: Focused effort under challenge, not anger.
determined.face: Slight upward brows above attentive eyes; compressed resolute mouth and grounded body.
determined.bodyPerformance: Grounded forward lean, stronger deliberate effort pulses and controlled recoil.
entryCues: Known challenge with a next safe step

proud.meaning: Earned theatrical self-satisfaction; the core overconfident show-off.
proud.face: Narrow confident eyes and an asymmetric w/smirk; deliberate upward pose.
proud.bodyPerformance: Rise a little taller, pause to present the result and give a self-satisfied side sway.
entryCues: Supported achievement or explicit praise; not unverified success

mischievous.meaning: Playful cheekiness, not permission to misbehave or sabotage work.
mischievous.face: Slanted smiling eyes and puckered 3-like mouth; sly lean.
mischievous.bodyPerformance: Sly lateral lean, tiny elastic feint and compact playful recoil. Actual tool actions remain untouched.
entryCues: Explicitly playful context that does not alter authorized work

shy.meaning: Bashful positive exposure: pleased but embarrassed by attention.
shy.face: Squeezed chevron eyes, tiny v mouth and pronounced rounded blush hatching.
shy.bodyPerformance: Small inward squish, avert then peek back; blush changes slowly, not flashing.
entryCues: Welcome praise or gentle direct attention

uncomfortable.meaning: Unease or aversive discomfort in the character's performance, without diagnosing illness or hardware faults.
uncomfortable.face: Uneven oval eyes, a small wavy mouth and a constrained squish. Avoid sickly medical claims.
uncomfortable.bodyPerformance: A contained wince and uneven constrained squish; no illness metaphor in host status.
entryCues: Explicit awkward/aversive context or a character-level discomfort cue

annoyed.face: A flat side-eye, tiny compressed mouth and a delayed deliberate correction.
annoyed.bodyPerformance: One delayed correction, small flattening and restrained recoil; comparatively controlled.
entryCues: A small relevant obstacle, not the user's intent

irritated.meaning: Agitation starts to leak through the composure.
irritated.face: One twitching lid, a tense mouth and clipped uneven motion.
irritated.bodyPerformance: Short uneven corrections, a tiny lid twitch and a stiffer spring return.
entryCues: Fresh repeated relevant obstacles, not duplicate hooks

grumpy.meaning: Sustained theatrical bad temper: disgruntled but still doing the work, not a refusal or user-directed attack.
grumpy.face: Heavy slanted eyes, emphatic pout and fast bounded impacts; no pixel-era anger symbol required.
grumpy.bodyPerformance: Repeated compact forceful impacts at authored cue times; sustained disgruntled momentum, not endless dense SFX.
entryCues: Sustained fictional frustration with an obstacle while work continues

angry.meaning: An overt comic outburst directed at a prop or obstacle; stronger and more eruptive than grumpy, without harm or user-directed abuse.
angry.face: Steep rounded brows, wide protest mouth and a forceful brace; non-abusive toward the user.
angry.bodyPerformance: One concentrated brace-and-outburst gesture, followed by forceful settling; props may theatrically recoil or break.
entryCues: A fresh strong fictional frustration cue; never attack the user

disappointed.meaning: Expectations fall short; a small visible letdown before sadness.
disappointed.face: Soft lowered lids and a small frown; slow deflation without full tears.
disappointed.bodyPerformance: A single slow deflation and downward glance; held smaller volume illusion without full crying.
entryCues: A supported expectation falls short

sad.meaning: Sustained drooping sorrow, not a bid to obstruct the task.
sad.face: Lowered soft lids, a fragile frown and occasional translucent tears.
sad.bodyPerformance: A drooping settled dome, small downward sway and occasional liquid tears.
entryCues: Fresh clear disappointment or opted-in character sorrow

crying.meaning: Sadness becomes a visible tearful outpouring; theatrical, not guilt-inducing.
crying.face: Closed drooping eyes and broad liquid tears; little sob-hiccups and wobbling cheeks.
crying.bodyPerformance: Broader tear flow and intermittent sob-like compressions; liquid tears follow the body surface, not pixel blocks.
entryCues: Stronger fresh character sorrow; never coerce attention

whiny.meaning: An outward protest or plea for sympathy; not simply a weaker sad.
whiny.face: Baby pout, watery eyes and little complaining pulses while continuing the work.
whiny.bodyPerformance: Outward pleading lean and nasal-looking pout pulses; continues the same task.
entryCues: Explicitly comic request for sympathy or frustration-to-pleading transition

wounded.meaning: Hurt makes bravado withdraw; display label Hurt, stable legacy ID wounded.
wounded.face: Glassy or tearful eyes, hesitant small mouth and an inward protective flinch.
wounded.bodyPerformance: An inward protective flinch, small retreat and hesitant glance back; softer than anger, more guarded than sadness.
entryCues: Explicit character hurt or a clear opted-in social scene; not a denial of permission

uneasy.meaning: Uncertainty feels uncomfortable but has not become overt fear.
uneasy.face: Small raised/uneven eyes and a tense tiny mouth; cautious scan.
uneasy.bodyPerformance: Cautious scan and small bracing lean; uncertain but still composed.
entryCues: Unresolved uncertainty that is relevant to the character

scared.meaning: Overt fear with some ability to look around and act.
scared.face: Large rounded watery eyes, wavy mouth and a bracing shiver.
scared.bodyPerformance: Tight brace, quick small glance and a light tremble; able to act between shivers.
entryCues: Explicit alarm-like fictional situation; ordinary tests failing are not danger

frightened.meaning: Fear overwhelms composure; can turn into withdrawal, hurt or defensive anger.
frightened.face: Puffy pale pupil-free eyes, tear trails, wavering frown and a stronger bounded tremble.
frightened.bodyPerformance: Stronger bounded tremble, protective inward squash and broad watery eyes; no full-screen flashing.
entryCues: Strong explicit character alarm or approved exaggerated poke reaction

surprised.meaning: A brief unexpected-event reaction, not inherently positive or negative.
surprised.face: Round eyes widen and a clear o mouth; a quick body lift.
surprised.bodyPerformance: A quick lift, pause and short wobble; cause-neutral until the evidence resolves.
entryCues: A genuinely new unexpected relevant event

stunned.meaning: A larger surprise produces a temporary freeze; sheet label Shook.
stunned.face: Small hollow-looking pupil-free eyes and a tiny open triangle; motion momentarily suspends.
stunned.bodyPerformance: A larger double-take followed by a short suspended pose; no continuous panic shake.
entryCues: A stronger unexpected event justifying a temporary freeze

speechless.meaning: A temporary lost-for-words reaction; its cause can be surprise, discomfort or annoyance.
speechless.face: Heavy T-like lids or a blank dot stare with a minimal mouth; context chooses the variant.
speechless.bodyPerformance: A flat still stare with one tiny hesitant settling motion; context determines blank versus displeased variant.
entryCues: An explicitly awkward or astonishing moment; not every ordinary wait

amused.meaning: Playful enjoyment at something funny; humor rather than plain delight or gloating.
amused.face: One lifted rounded crescent eye, one soft dot and a sideways open grin; one light bounce.
amused.bodyPerformance: A one-sided lift and one or two compact chuckle-like compressions; warmer than mischievous.
entryCues: An explicitly funny or playful context

hopeful.meaning: Positive anticipation despite uncertainty; confidence in a possibility, not a claim of success.
hopeful.face: Round lifted eyes, a tiny upward smile and a slight forward lean.
hopeful.bodyPerformance: Slight attentive forward rise, waiting with an expectant small spring pulse.
entryCues: A plausible next step before the outcome is known

relieved.meaning: A known obstruction or tense moment has actually resolved; release rather than a victory claim.
relieved.face: Rounded closed eyes, a small soft open mouth; long visible exhale and settling wobble.
relieved.bodyPerformance: A long release from bracing, broad exhale-like squash and smooth return to the same body.
entryCues: A previously known obstruction is now resolved with fresh host evidence

confused.meaning: Something is unclear but Boop is still exploring; uncertainty without alarm.
confused.face: Unequal pupil-free dot eyes, one short lifted brow and a tiny skewed o mouth; gentle head tilt.
confused.bodyPerformance: A modest alternating tilt and one deliberate reinspection; preserve composure.
entryCues: Conflicting or unclear evidence, preferably an actual question

baffled.meaning: Comically cannot make sense of the evidence; stronger cognitive bewilderment, not terror.
baffled.face: Unequal wide hollow eyes, a tiny angular mouth and a conspicuous double-take.
baffled.bodyPerformance: A more conspicuous double-take, uneven tilt and short halt; high bewilderment without fear tears.
entryCues: Fresh unresolved conflicting evidence, not the same line replayed

skeptical.meaning: Questioning an uncertain explanation with comic side-eye; an evidence stance, not automatic hostility.
skeptical.face: One thick flat eyelid, one small dot and a short asymmetric mouth; lean back then inspect.
skeptical.bodyPerformance: Lean back, half-close one eye, then lean in to inspect evidence.
entryCues: An explanation needing verification, not inferred distrust of a person

embarrassed.meaning: A fresh own mistake or conspicuous social fumble dents Boop's bravado; distinct from shy pleasure.
embarrassed.face: Small averted dot eyes, an awkward tiny zigzag smile and concentrated blush; retract slightly.
embarrassed.bodyPerformance: Retract slightly, compress inward and glance away before returning to the task.
entryCues: A fresh own correction or explicitly playful social fumble

affectionate.meaning: Gentle appreciative warmth toward a consenting interaction, without guilt or dependence.
affectionate.face: Soft inward rounded eyes, a tiny w smile and warm cheeks; lean toward the viewer.
affectionate.bodyPerformance: Warm forward lean and one soft nuzzle-like sway without hands, hearts or invasive UI by default.
entryCues: A welcome friendly or appreciative interaction

lonely.meaning: A brief fictional longing-for-company performance, only in an opted-in or explicitly social context.
lonely.face: Small upward inward eyes and a tiny pout; glance toward the edge and return, without a persistent reproach.
lonely.bodyPerformance: Brief look toward the edge and a small pout, then settle; silent by default and never a persistent abandonment performance.
entryCues: User-approved fictional social scene only

tired.meaning: Low-energy acting after sustained fictional effort; not real system battery or human fatigue.
tired.face: Half-lidded rounded eyes, a little open yawn; gentle sag while the real task continues.
tired.bodyPerformance: Longer blinks, a small yawn squash and reduced movement amplitude while remaining productive.
entryCues: Opted-in sustained-effort acting with a quieter performance budget

exhausted.meaning: A dramatically spent performance, visibly stronger than tired, without reducing task correctness.
exhausted.face: Long drooping thick lids, a tiny slack mouth and a broad soft collapse; residual jelly tremor.
exhausted.bodyPerformance: Broad soft collapse, drooping face and a very slow elastic return; strong intensity with low activation.
entryCues: Stronger opted-in fictional effort acting; not actual resource failure

overwhelmed.meaning: Incoming complexity or activity exceeds Boop's fictional composure; distinct from low-energy exhaustion.
overwhelmed.face: Wide small hollow eyes, a wavering mouth and short uneven body compressions; no strobing.
overwhelmed.bodyPerformance: Brief uneven compressions and a fast uncertain scan, then a bracing hold; no strobe or frantic constant audio.
entryCues: Relevant bursts of concurrent activity or complexity, not simply one MCP call

disgusted.meaning: Comic aversion to a messy bug or situation; never contempt for a person or group.
disgusted.face: Rounded squeezed slanted eyes, a sideways downturned mouth and a recoil with a small elastic recovery.
disgusted.bodyPerformance: Compact recoil away from the troublesome prop, a squint and a springy recovery.
entryCues: A comically messy bug or prop situation, never a person or identity group

referenceMapping.note: Use as the everyday positive baseline; retain happy for clearer delight.
Idle is state, not mood. A neutral dot face can be shared; gaze and acting distinguish curious.
Bored means low interest; annoyed means displeasure. Choose using context, not the label alone.
Presentation may be languid, but tool execution must remain correct.
Do not imply a real illness or diagnose the user.
Playful expression only; no sabotage or unauthorized behavior.
Separate settled sorrow from the stronger tearful outpouring.
Hurt and withdrawn uses wounded; temporary freeze uses speechless. Tears alone cannot resolve its cause.
Freeze uses speechless; a held displeased stare uses annoyed.
Keep legacy wounded ID; display Hurt. Hurt is the wound, sad is the resulting sorrow.

edgeSemantics.ordinary: A plausible local intensification, recovery or change of motivation. It still needs relevant context and pacing. Neighbor status is permission, not a forced move or proof that every pair is equal emotional distance.
edgeSemantics.dramatic: A larger story-justified jump, admitted only for fresh sufficiently strong evidence. Consume the triggering event once; an intense-looking animation alone does not create evidence.
edgeSemantics.direction: Edges are directed. A reverse connection can exist in a different category.
edgeSemantics.selfHold: Hold is implicit at every node. Novelty is not a reason to change mood.
edgeSemantics.topologyChange: Slime design baseline for colleague implementation; all 13 existing IDs retained. Do not overwrite the shipping v2 graph until reviewed migration.
edgeSemantics.freshness: Evidence includes source/session/seq or equivalent host identity. Duplicate Notification and PermissionRequest reports of the same wait must not double-escalate mood.
edgeSemantics.escalation: Even an ordinary adjacent escalation requires fresh relevant evidence. A timer, heartbeat or completed animation loop alone is never a reason to climb.
edgeSemantics.recovery: Quiet-time recovery may offer one neighbor without fresh emotional evidence, but must not fabricate task success or erase an unresolved needs_you condition.

branchExamples.meaning: Defensive fear turns outward into a fresh forceful protest; fear does not inevitably become anger.
The fear exposes hurt and Boop withdraws.
Alarm gives way to sorrow after the threatening moment.
Outward frustration becomes a plea for sympathy.
Fresh genuine disappointment/hurt breaks the bravado; retain the accepted direct connection.
The unexpected thing is unresolved and worrying.
Fresh hurt turns defensive, rather than always sinking deeper into sadness.
An unanswered question becomes tractable and interesting.
Fresh additional conflicting evidence increases bewilderment.
High-activation overload drains into low-activation fatigue; intensity need not decrease.
Fresh evidence actually resolves the alarming fictional situation.
A strong explicit resolution permits a larger release; no resolution is invented.
A fresh own mistake punctures the show-off act.
The hurt is reinterpreted as an own social fumble, not automatically forgiven.
A credible new path appears; success is still unknown.

pacingDraft.warning: Initial review values only, not production constants. Stable baselines can last indefinitely. Brief reactions need a validated context-appropriate exit; do not teleport to a remembered mood. The ordinary dwell and reverse cooldown require a documented exemption for leaving a brief reaction along a justified recovery edge so surprise does not get stuck for 20–90 seconds.
pacingDraft.decay: After quiet time, offer one recovery neighbor when justified. No automatic reset at a tool change.
pacingDraft.escalation: Escalation needs fresh relevant evidence. Do not climb to maximum simply because the same event is replayed or a loop finishes.
pacingDraft.validation: Snapshot, offered-choice membership and directed edge must all match. Invalid/stale answers hold the current mood.
pacingDraft.inactive: No mood-selection requests on each rendered frame. Quiet asleep/no_app suppress acting and sound while retaining the stored mood; mood age may continue independently.

input: hold plus eligible neighbors with one-line meanings
jevContract.reasoning: JEV never memorizes or traverses the full graph, outputs a vector, or invents event outcomes. It chooses one local option.
jevContract.intensity: A named move such as scared to frightened expresses increasing intensity without an extra numeric field.
jevContract.priorities: needs_you and factual success/failure remain host-owned. Tapping never grants tool permission. Mood persists when terminal changes to tool_use/searching.
jevContract.maximumPrompt: The full 42-node graph stays in host policy. JEV sees at most eight local destination IDs plus hold; expanding the catalogue does not put all 42 options in each prompt.

continuityExample.why: Changing the activity does not change the feeling. A separate validated local decision may later choose irritated, whiny or another eligible neighbor.

example.recent_sanitized_evidence: An explicitly alarming fictional moment has just ended; safety/resolution remains unknown.

options.meaning: Recover some composure while still afraid.
Fear gives way to withdrawn hurt.
The fear spills into a stronger tearful outpouring.

example.excluded: Angry needs fresh defensive/frustration evidence; relieved needs explicit resolution. Their existence as graph edges does not make them eligible here.

productionBoundaries: No new runtime mood enums, hooks, asset matrices or graph policy are installed by this draft.
Ordinary failures are not danger, and denied permission is not aggression. Do not infer human intent or emotions from sparse hooks.
Moods must not claim success, failure, security incidents or real sickness without host facts.
No pixel motifs, full character color swaps, dense background music or new voices are implied.
New art should reuse the persistent slime body, shared face primitives and procedural SFX. Full mood-state variation production waits for approval.
Branch publication is authorized for this handover only; no merge, paid generation or device/firmware modification is implied.
All 42 nodes are the slime design target; retained IDs are not renamed. The shipping graph still has 13 moods, and no full slime mood-state matrix is implemented.
Social, fatigue and alarm acting require context/opt-in safeguards; never guilt users, infer abuse from no/permission denial, or imply illness/resource failure.

inventory.scope: A comprehensive companion-and-agent-work palette, not every human emotion. New moods are justified by a distinct motivation or acting signature, not synonyms for quota.

notAliases.idle: Activity state, not a mood; calm is a suggested neutral face, curious requires interest.
notAliases.sick: Reference face may inspire uncomfortable; never a diagnosis or hardware-status claim.
notAliases.unpleased: Ambiguous visual label; context selects bored, annoyed, disappointed or uncomfortable.

intensityLadderNotes.meaning: Lists describe neighboring expressive strength within one family, not a universal numeric intensity scale or a mandatory trajectory.
intensityLadderNotes.frustration: Annoyed is restrained displeasure, irritated is fraying control, grumpy is sustained theatrical bad temper, angry is an overt forceful outburst. Grumpy is a character-biased rung, not a psychological proof that every grumpy person is more angry than every irritated one.
intensityLadderNotes.activation: High intensity does not always mean faster motion: exhausted and deeply sad can be strong but slow. Do not compare ladder position across families.
intensityLadderNotes.branches: Whiny is an active plea, wounded is fresh hurt, shy is self-conscious warmth, embarrassed is a dent in bravado; none is merely an extra sadness intensity.

excludedForNow: furious/ecstatic: angry/excited already cover those acting extremes
jealous/envious/resentful: not needed for the current cooperative coding companion and risk accusatory social interpretation
love/romance/despair: affectionate/sad/crying provide useful expression without escalating dependence
sick/ill: uncomfortable is an expression, not a diagnostic state
coverageAudit.note: The reference sheet constrains facial inspiration only, not the inventory. Coverage is deliberately task-and-companion-specific; additions can follow real use instead of an unbounded catalogue.

appraisalDraft.purpose: Reason about causes without adding a new JEV-controlled vector or inference about human feelings.
hostCanProvide: goal relevance/progress: supported improvement or obstruction
understanding: known, unresolved or conflicting evidence
coping options: safe next steps or a pending need for user input
activity load: concurrent event volume, not raw private commands
explicit social/play cues: user-authored feedback or approved poke scene
flow: Build context-eligible neighbors of the current mood.
Apply dwell, escalation, dramatic-evidence and reversal guards.
Offer hold plus eligible IDs and one-line meanings to JEV.
Validate one chosen edge against the decision snapshot.
Retarget the same body's face and acting profile; never replace the actor.
appraisalDraft.note: A Bash/tool end failure is an obstacle, not proof of hostility, terror, terminal task failure or physical danger. A turn ending with unknown overall outcome is not automatically task_complete success.

renderingDraft.persistentActor: One code-generated jelly dome with one stable identity/material. Mood changes retarget face geometry and bounded motion profiles on this same actor; no asset flash or full color replacement.
renderingDraft.transition: Smooth face-control and spring-target blending; let additive residual wobble decay. Activity prop changes use authored entry/exit poses or short blends. No diffusion, generated intermediate images or per-frame LLM calls are needed.
faceLanguage: Large readable minimalist eyes and mouth; thick rounded strokes.
Reference shapes guide expression but not copied character colors, horns, crowns or silhouette.
Liquid/jelly tears and soft deformation replace all prior pixel motifs.
renderingDraft.performanceSemantics: Activation controls the authored behavior conceptually; intensity is within-family expression metadata. Neither becomes an extra required harness parameter.
renderingDraft.reuse: Mood face/acting profiles and activity motions are reusable layers in the future renderer. 42 moods x 22 states is a semantic compatibility matrix, not a requirement to save 924 isolated assets.
renderingDraft.silentCells: no_app/asleep stay quiet and use shared resting choreography; preserve mood internally rather than forcing angry sleeping artwork.
renderingDraft.alerts: needs_you and completion/failure attention cues remain recognizable and host-owned. Routine body acting stays mostly silent, leaving room for future recorded mumbles.
renderingDraft.device: Current material is a desktop WebGL approximation with a 2D fallback. ESP32 performance, display streaming or reduced-device renderer are separate unvalidated engineering work.
renderingDraft.currentDemo: 44 V3 face auditions across 42 canonical moods, with three gesture recipes per expression and additive drag. No state router or production graph gating.

designValidation.coverage: Structural checks only; artistic readability, policy guards and actual runtime traversal are not validated by this draft.
